seo.title: AI File Organizer — Organize Local Files With Preview and Approval

items.question: Does organizing local files mean no data leaves my device?
items.answer: No. File operations can take place locally while selected content is sent to a model or connected service. Check the provider, tool permissions, and material involved before using sensitive files; a local folder alone is not a privacy guarantee.

items.question: Can it rename and move files together?
items.answer: Yes. A single approved plan can create folders, rename files, and move them into the proposed structure while reporting the result per file.

items.question: What happens when the agent is unsure?
items.answer: Uncertain matches should be surfaced for review rather than silently forced into a category. You can correct the plan before execution.

items.question: Can I reuse an organization system?
items.answer: Yes. A successful rule can become a reusable workflow for recurring exports, client onboarding, downloads, or project archives.

items.question: How should possible duplicate files be handled?
items.answer: Keep deletion out of the first organization pass. Review content, version history, and project references before deciding that two similar names identify the same file; retain uncertain candidates for a separate check.

items.question: How can I avoid breaking references when renaming a project folder?
items.answer: Start with a small copy or noncritical subset, identify documents and applications that refer to the old paths, and review proposed moves before applying them. A cleaner folder tree is not useful if it breaks links or working project files.
